svg.title: NL2SQL Agent v8 architecture
svg.desc: v7's ensemble, read in the light of the conversation: the Supervisor restating a follow-up, held in code, and the generator shown the earlier turns; and the pipeline named by its release
svg.metadata: screen refuse paraphrase screen_paraphrase plan_wave answer validate judge vote fuse deliver
svg.text: NL2SQL Agent v8 — the question, read in its conversation
v7's two graphs, their nodes and edges unchanged, with a conversation behind them: a question asked in one is read with its last answered turns, and the release a deployment answers with is named.
Everything marked in rose is new in v8. The pipeline inside each run is drawn as one box here and node by node in arch_v5_6.svg; v7's own additions are drawn in arch_v7.svg.
DEPLOYMENT — WHAT RUNS WHERE
nl2sql-postgres
Postgres 18, the same 19 tables. v5 reads
two more things from it, once per process:
the key constraints every dimension
declares, which become the label map
(sku_id → product_name), and the latest
fiscal year the sales cover in full, which
becomes the default period.
← SQLAlchemy + psycopg · pg_trgm
nl2sql-vectordb
pgvector, the same stores as v3. The DDL
collection now has a reader: it is the Schema
Retriever's index, one chunk per table, and it
is excluded from the knowledge search so
no table is described twice.
← cosine search, DDL + knowledge + both pair fields
nl2sql-chunkdb
Plain Postgres, the context store.
golden_pairs holds the 45 question/SQL
pairs one row per pair — chunk_id, type,
tables, keywords, question,
reasoning_target, sql_code, result — beside
the BM25 term statistics over the keyword
column and the golden_pairs_bm25()
function that ranks against them.
← BM25 ranking + row hydration
nl2sql-snippetsdb
pgvector. The SQL snippets of
context_questions/sql_snippets.md -- joins,
filters, measures, dimensions -- with a
keyword matcher over their phrases and an
embedding of each meaning. Read as a role
that can SELECT and nothing else.
← keyword phrases + cosine, as snippets_reader
conversations — in memory
Kept by the REST API's process, never on
disk: per person and per id the page or the
window made, the last
CONVERSATION_MEMORY (5) answered
turns -- each the question answered, three
rows of its answer, its SQL. One question at
a time a conversation; forgotten idle after an
hour, on DELETE, or for a turn marked
wrong.
→ the turns a question is read with
Ollama — chat models, gated
The same routed models. Every routed call
now waits for a slot at the host gate:
OLLAMA_PARALLEL_CALLS of them, one
by default, process-wide -- so the runs of a
question go one after another on a host that
serves one call at a time, and side by side
only on the deployer's word.
→ every call through the gate
Ollama — embedding model
bge-m3 on the machine running Docker,
reached as host.docker.internal via
extra_hosts: host-gateway. 1024
dimensions. Three of the four retrievers
embed the question; only the two vector
searches over the golden pairs share one
call.
→ one embed_query per retriever
models/catalog.json
Schema 3: seven tasks. The Paraphraser
and the Judge are calibrated beside the five;
a schema-2 catalog is still read, the two
tasks unmeasured and routed to
OLLAMA_MODEL.
← read once, at startup
nl2sql-agent
python -m nl2sql_agent, or the same image serving
the REST API, which keeps the conversations.
PIPELINE_VERSION names the pipeline: v7_0_0 the
outer graph drawn here, v6_3_1 one run of the
pipeline inside it.
What v8 adds: the conversation

A follow-up -- "and in each state?" -- names nothing, so asked alone it is refused or answered as something else. v8 reads it with the conversation's last answered turns, at two places and nowhere else.
The Supervisor reads the words typed in their light and restates a follow-up so that it stands alone; code then holds the restatement to the words typed -- C1 every number, C2 every quoted value, C3

every direction, C4 its shape -- and discards it otherwise, with no model call. The restatement, when it held, is the question every later stage answers, and the words typed are kept beside it everywhere.

The SQL Generator is shown the earlier turns' questions and SQL after its worked examples, since a follow-up usually keeps their joins, filters and calendar. Everything in rose is new in v8: no node is
added to either graph, and with no turns every prompt is v7's, byte for byte.
The pipeline by name
PIPELINE_VERSION names the pipeline a deployment answers with, so two releases can be compared by name. v7_0_0, the default, is this drawing: every question asked several ways. v6_3_1 is the
ensemble off and nothing else -- one run of the pipeline inside, the grain check and the conversation still applying -- so a comparison of the two names measures one difference. ENSEMBLE_ENABLED
unset follows the name; set, it is what was said, and true under v6_3_1 is refused at start.
What it costs

A question asked in a conversation, with turns to read, costs one Supervisor call more: the reading in context at the standard rung, then v7's screening of the words it settled on. A question asked alone,
or with CONVERSATION_MEMORY=0, costs what it did in v7, call for call.
THE ENSEMBLE — AN OUTER LANGGRAPH STATEGRAPH AROUND THE PIPELINE
state: EnsembleState (TypedDict) · question is the standalone reading, asked the words typed, turns what was remembered
START
screen
reads the turns
The Supervisor, on the question as typed. In a conversation, first a
reading in the light of its last answered turns, restating a follow-up so
that it stands alone, held in code to every number, quoted value and
direction typed; then v7's screening of the words it settled on: verdict,
intent and the answer contract.
LLM · Supervision
+1 call with turns
C1-C4 · code
WHY
Memory enters here and the generator only. The Supervisor screens the words typed, so an
injection hidden in a follow-up is screened as typed; and a restatement is model output about to
become every later stage's question, so code holds it to what the person wrote before anything
runs. A follow-up that stood alone already is left as it was, which is why a question asked alone
is answered as v7 answered it.
refuse
Answer with the scope sentence,
the refusal or the clarifying
question, and stop. Nothing is
reworded and nothing runs. →
END
terminal · exit 0
WHY
Exactly v5.6's refusal, reached one graph further out. Nothing was reworded and nothing ran,
so the record says level none with no candidates, and a client shows the refusal as it always
did.
paraphrase
The Paraphraser. One structured call: up to
ENSEMBLE_MAX_PARAPHRASES (10) rewordings of the question,
each different from it and from the others, each with a few words on
what was changed.
LLM · Rewordings
routed: the Supervisor's rung
WHY
One call for all of them, so the rewordings are written to differ from each other, the most
different first. The Paraphraser is told what must not change in words -- the entities, the
measure, the period, the limit -- and is never shown the contract as the generator sees it:
shown a column name, it copies the column name into the question, and the wordings stop
being a person's.
screen_paraphrase
The fidelity gate, a rewording at a time. In code: F1 the same numbers,
F2 the same literals, F3 the same direction, F5 distinct from the
question and the others. Then F4: the Supervisor reads it, and its
reading must build the anchor's contract. Too few faithful, and the
Paraphraser is asked once more.
F1 F2 F3 F5 · code
F4 · LLM per rewording
discarded, never run
WHY
A rewording is model output about to become a prompt, so it is checked like one. F1 to F3 and
F5 are code and cost nothing, so they run first; F4 is the Supervisor reading the rewording,
which makes it the injection screen for text a model wrote, and its reading must build the
anchor's contract. A rewording that asks something else is discarded with the check it failed,
never run -- an answer to a different question would vote.
plan_wave
Which wordings run now. The first wave: the question as asked,
candidate 0, and the first ENSEMBLE_PARAPHRASES (3) faithful
rewordings. The second, when there is one: the faithful rewordings not
yet run.
no model call
ENSEMBLE_WAVES · 2
WHY
The original is always candidate 0: whatever the rewordings do, the question as asked is
among the runs. The second wave is planned only when the first could not settle the vote, from
rewordings already written and already checked, so it costs runs and no new rewording.
answer
The candidate runs: each wording through the whole v5.6 pipeline,
seeded with the anchor's screening and contract.
OLLAMA_PARALLEL_CALLS runs at a time -- one by default -- each
reading as the same database role, each with its own state, trace and
attempts.
the v5.6 pipeline, once per wording
generate_sql shown the turns
host gate
WHY
Each run is the whole pipeline with its own repair loop and its own seven attempts, in a copied
context so its progress and its trace spans stay its own. Runs share no state: the only thing one
run knows of another is the contract they were all seeded with. A run that gives up is a run that
could not answer, and the vote goes on without it.
Inside each run: the v5.6 pipeline's nodes, and the grain check
supervise (handed the anchor's screening, so no model call) → the five
retrievers → aggregate → generate_sql (shown the earlier turns, after
the worked examples) → validate_static (with the grain check) →
planner_gate → execute_query → review → visualise → narrate → audit
→ finish, with its one repair loop and one attempts counter. Nineteen
nodes, none added and none renamed: drawn node by node in
arch_v5_6.svg.
validate
Per run, E1 to E5: it answered; its wording passed the fidelity gate; it
has rows where the question implies some; the audit found no semantic
issue; and its rows are the whole result, not a sample cut at the row
cap. Then every pair of admissible results is compared, and the runs fall
into groups: one group, one answer.
no model call
the benchmark's scorer
WHY
Two questions, in order. Is this result an answer to its own question -- answered, with rows,
audited, whole -- and only then: which results are the same answer. Sameness is the
benchmark's own scorer, so two queries that differ in column names, column order or rounding
agree, and two that return different numbers do not, whatever their SQL looks like.
judge
The Judge, once a wave. It is shown each distinct answer by letter --
the query and its first five rows, the original's first -- with the question,
what every answer was held to and the knowledge, and gives a verdict
for each: accepted, or set aside with the mistake in one sentence.
LLM · Verdicts
routed: heavy, always
never told the count
WHY
Runs that make the same mistake get the same number, and so they agree: without this, a
majority can be wrong together. The Judge reads the answers before they are counted and is
never told how many runs gave each, so it cannot side with the crowd. It may set an answer
aside only for a mistake it can point to in the query, it cannot write SQL, and it cannot take the
answer away: with none accepted the runs' own choice is delivered, flagged.
vote
Over the runs whose answer the Judge accepted: the largest group
wins, a strict majority of the voters settles it, and the level is recorded --
unanimous, majority, judged, contested or single. Unsettled, with a
wave left and inside the deadline when one is set: back to plan_wave.
no model call
→ plan_wave when unsettled
WHY
The level is the confidence a reader is given: every voter agreed, most did, the Judge overruled
the runs' own choice, nothing had a majority, or one run stood alone. An unsettled vote with a
wave left goes round again; a settled one never does, so a question that four wordings agree
on costs four runs and not eleven.
fuse
Choose the winning group's representative -- complete, audited, the
original before a rewording, fewest attempts, cheapest plan. Join the
columns the other members carry, add their claims about rows not yet
spoken of, unite the assumptions, describe each answer that lost, and
write the agreement line.
no model call
columns: on, and a switch
SQL is never merged
WHY
Selection first: one run's query is the answer's query, chosen by a fixed ranking, and SQL is
never merged. What fusion adds is what the other agreeing runs carry that the chosen one
lacks -- a column, joined only when every row matches exactly once on the entity's key, and
named with the run it came from; a claim about rows not yet spoken of, re-verified against the
rows. The answer that lost is described from the two queries' trees, not by a model.
deliver
Read as
Render the answer: "Read as: ..." when a follow-up was restated, the
agreement line, the claims, the table, then the notes. With no run to
deliver, the original's own ending. The answer becomes a turn of its
conversation. → END
no model call
Answer.conversation
WHY
One answer, with how it was arrived at beside it rather than instead of it. A client written for v5.6
reads the same fields it always did; one written for v7 reads the record too.
END
second wave · only when the vote is unsettled
OUTCOMES
unanimous
Every run that voted gave this answer.
majority
Most did; the others are named among
the notes, with how their query differs.
judged
The Judge set aside the answer the
runs preferred, and this is the one it
accepted.
contested
No majority, or the Judge accepted
none: the runs' own choice, flagged.
single
One run's answer stands alone.

The level opens the answer as a sentence -- "Agreed by 4 of 4 independent runs of the question, each worded differently" -- and is what a client shows as a badge. A question refused at the anchor has level none: nothing ran.
WHAT THE SURFACES SHOW
The terminal
The interactive session is one
conversation; a follow-up prints "Read
as"; a question on the command line is
asked alone.
--memory · --pipeline
The REST API
A request names its conversation; the
answer says its turn and how it was
read; 409 while one runs; DELETE
forgets it.
Answer.conversation
Web and desktop
An id per page or window, a New
conversation button, "Read as" under a
follow-up, and the status bar saying
what is remembered.
id · button · Read as
MLflow
The pipeline, conversation, turn,
remembered and resolved tags; the
Supervisor's span shows the turns it
was given.
nl2sql.conversation
Review
A follow-up is staged as the question
answered, and the words typed are
shown beside it; a wrong verdict
forgets the turn.
asked as
control flow
second wave
model call
database access
new in v8
v5.6's pipeline
